tools.tool: UTILITY REPORT / VERIFY / CLEARANCE / CHECK (Survey > Subsurface Utilities: Report, Verify, Clearance, Check tabs)
tools.surfaces: window: utility dialog tabs plus typed UTILITY; cli: UTILITY verb; mcp: katana_run_commands only
tools.actsOn: A schedule CSV file only, plus design.csv and schema.csv. Never the drawing, not even the services UTILITY DRAW put there.
tools.missing: window: no scope and no filter (the dialog has only file fields and refuses a line without a schedule); cli: no scope and no filter, file only; mcp: no scope and no filter, and no structured tool
tools.evidence: src/katana_cad/utilities/utility_verbs.cpp:81-92 readSchedule is the only source; report 165-183, verify 185-195, clearance 197-234 (design only from parseDesignCsv at 215), check 236-262 (checkDelivery over the raw file text at 253). src/katana_qt/survey/utility_dialog.cpp:125-131: utilityCommandLine requires a schedule file. src/katana_qt/survey/utility_dialog.hpp:26-47: the objectName list has no scope controls. src/katana_cad/utilities/utility_drawing.cpp:119-147: the points UTILITY DRAW writes lack the horizontal and vertical uncertainty, the depth and each segment's path evidence (UtilityVertex and PositionEvidence in utility_network.hpp:115-137 and quality_level.hpp:104-109), so a drawn service cannot be graded again as it stands.
tools.proposal: Keep the file as one source and add the drawing as a second (CLAUDE.md 1.1). Grammar: UTILITY REPORT|VERIFY|CHECK [<schedule.csv> | <scope> [WHERE ...]] ... ; no file means the shared scope clause, defaulting to SELECTION. Examples: 'UTILITY REPORT LAYERS utilities', 'UTILITY REPORT VIEW WHERE PROP=utility.type:water'. (1) New cad::utilities::utilityLinesFrom(document, ids) rebuilds sub::UtilityLine from the matched entities that carry utility.line: points are the vertices, in order; polylines carry the attributes. Matched entities that are not drawn services are counted and named. (2) UTILITY DRAW first writes what a regrade needs: utility.h_uncertainty, utility.v_uncertainty, utility.depth, utility.path (evidence of the segment that starts at this vertex) and utility.seq (vertex order). The acceptance test is that REPORT on the drawn services equals REPORT on the file they were drawn from. (3) CLEARANCE takes DESIGN <file.csv> | DESIGN <id> | DESIGN <scope>; a polyline's vertices, with levels from entity::heightsOf, become the DesignAlignment. (4) CHECK uses a new checkDelivery overload over rows (column to value), built from the utility.field.* properties plus the interpreted keys mapped back to schema attribute names. (5) The reply starts 'matched=N services=M not_utilities=K', and an empty scope is reported, not refused. (6) Window: the dialog gets a Source choice (utilitySourceFile, utilitySourceDrawing) and the shared ScopeFilterWidget (utilityScope), and still only builds the line. (7) MCP: through the verb; optionally the shared scope/where JSON (T27).

tools.tool: UTILITY DRAW (draw again, or regrade, what is already drawn)
tools.surfaces: window: dialog Draw tab plus typed; cli; mcp via run_commands
tools.actsOn: A schedule file, turned into new entities. Services already in the drawing cannot be regraded or redrawn after an edit. LAYER takes a prefix only.
tools.missing: window, cli and mcp: no drawing source (a scope), and no replacement of what the scope took
tools.evidence: src/katana_cad/utilities/utility_verbs.cpp:268-296. include/katana/cad/utilities/utility_drawing.hpp: utilityDrawCommand only adds entities and reuses layers.
tools.proposal: 'UTILITY DRAW <scope> [WHERE ...] REGRADE [SPACING m] [MINCOVER m]' rebuilds UtilityLines from the matched drawn services (utility_source from T01) and replaces those entities in one undo step (delete what matched, add the new drawing). The file form is unchanged. The reply is the same 'utilities drawn ...' record, preceded by 'matched=N'.

tools.tool: SELECT verb (also Edit > Select All, which runs SELECT ALL)
tools.surfaces: window: typed plus Select All; cli; mcp: run_commands only
tools.actsOn: ALL | NONE | ids | LAYER name (exact, no sublayers) | TYPE name. One criterion, the document rule, and it always replaces the selection.
tools.missing: window, cli and mcp: VIEW, AREA (so no headless window select), LAYERS a,b with or without sublayers, the WHERE filter (style, colour, property=value, text, drawn), and ADD/REMOVE; the reply does not say what was left out. mcp: no katana_select tool.
tools.evidence: src/katana_cad/command_interpreter.cpp:1269-1336 uses its own SelectionFilter (1278-1316) and kNoLayerOverrides (1283); help text at 358. src/katana_qt/main_window.cpp:1799-1802: selectAll runs 'SELECT ALL'. include/katana/cad/selection.hpp:19-28: SelectionFilter is a second, smaller filter type.
tools.proposal: 'SELECT [ADD|REMOVE] <scope> [WHERE ...]' goes through the shared parser and matchEntities, then the document's isSelectable rule. What that rule leaves out is counted: '12 matched, 10 selected, 2 on locked or hidden layers'. Compatibility: SELECT LAYER x means LAYERS x ONLY, SELECT TYPE t means DRAWING WHERE TYPE=t, SELECT ALL means DRAWING. SelectionFilter stays for viewport picks only. This verb matters most: every selection verb and tool can reach any scope through it before gaining its own clause.

tools.tool: MOVE COPY ROTATE SCALE MIRROR ARRAY ERASE verbs
tools.surfaces: window: typed (menu Erase runs ERASE); cli; mcp: run_commands
tools.actsOn: The selection only (requireSelection).
tools.missing: window, cli and mcp: every scope and every filter; today the only route is SELECT first, and SELECT lacks view, area and where
tools.evidence: src/katana_cad/command_interpreter.cpp:1076-1082: transform() calls requireSelection and takes document_.selection().ids(). Help at 352 says '(act on the selection)'.
tools.proposal: An optional scope clause before the arguments: 'MOVE [<scope>] [WHERE ...] dx,dy', 'ERASE LAYERS temp WHERE TYPE=text'. Entities on locked layers are counted and left, as Global Modify leaves them (a DRAWING scope can include them, unlike a selection). The reply is 'N matched, N moved; K on locked layers left'. One undo step.

tools.tool: CHLAYER, COLOR, STYLE APPLY, PROP LIST|SET|DELETE|RENAME

tools.actsOn: The selection only.

tools.proposal: Each verb accepts the scope clause. CHLAYER, COLOR, STYLE APPLY, PROP SET and PROP DELETE become planGlobalModify requests (SET LAYER=, COLOUR=, STYLE=, PROP=, UNPROP=), so they report and skip locked layers exactly as MODIFY does. PROP RENAME needs EntityModify.renameProperties, an extension of the shared mechanism (T30 package). 'PROP LIST <scope>' lists the properties of what matched.

Select Matches runs 'SELECT <the same clause>'.

Its options are [All/View/Layers/Where/Previous]; typed 'Layers survey/*,kerb ONLY' and 'Where TYPE=point PROP=code:TREE' go through the shared scope parser, resolve through matchEntities plus isSelectable, and the step's message says 'N matched'. tools.tool: Quick Select and Select Similar
tools.surfaces: window only (tools); no verb
tools.actsOn: Quick Select: a kind, a layer pattern, one condition, and Drawing or Selection. Select Similar: the whole drawing, matched against the seed.
tools.missing: window: View, Layers with or without sublayers, AREA, and the style, colour, text and drawn filters. This is a second scope and filter implementation. cli and mcp: no equivalent until SELECT gains WHERE (T03).
tools.evidence: src/katana_cad/tools/select_tools.cpp:240-270: matchesWildcard, a third wildcard matcher beside cad::matchesPattern (customisation/global_modify.cpp:364) and entity::globMatches (src/katana_entity/annotation.cpp:301). 272-380: its own Condition and meets(). 400: 'Look in [Drawing/Selection]'. 50-60: selectableWhere with kNoLayerOverrides.
tools.proposal: Quick Select becomes a front end to the shared mechanism: its questions build a ModifyScope and a ModifyFilter. Its numeric and not-equal comparisons (< > <= >= <>) move into ModifyFilter (T30), so SELECT, LIST and MODIFY gain them too, and matchesWildcard is deleted. Select Similar builds a ModifyFilter from the seed (types, layer, style, colour) and searches a scope the person chooses (default Drawing; options View and Layers). No new verb: the typed form is 'SELECT <scope> WHERE ...'.

packages.name: PK1 Utilities act on the drawing (the owner's explicit request)
packages.design: First, check branch utility-scope-core (worktree C:/GitHubProjects/Katana-wt/uscope-core). At this audit it sits at 8cd6a7a with no changes, so it is unclear whether the scope-core agent also covers the utilities; do not duplicate its work. Order: (a) UTILITY DRAW writes the round-trip keys (utility.seq, h_uncertainty, v_uncertainty, depth, path). (b) New utility_source.cpp: utilityLinesFrom(document, ids) turns matched entities into UtilityLines. The property test is that REPORT, VERIFY and CHECK on the drawn services give the same result as on the source CSV. (c) utility_verbs.cpp: each form accepts a file or the shared scope clause. CLEARANCE also takes DESIGN <id|scope>, and a checkDelivery row overload feeds CHECK. (d) The dialog gets the Source radio and the ScopeFilterWidget and still only builds the line; utility_workbench keeps framing DRAW. (e) REGRADE replaces what matched in one undo step. Replies begin 'matched=N'; an empty scope is reported, not refused. Tests: tests/cad/utilities (globbed) and test_utility_dialog.cpp. Documentation: docs/subsurface_utilities.md. Needs the shared parser and widget from the scope-core work. Shared hotspot: src/katana_cad/CMakeLists.txt:60 lists the utilities sources explicitly, so +utility_source.cpp there.

packages.name: PK2 Interpreter verbs on a scope: SELECT, LIST, INFO, the transforms, the attribute verbs, AREA, PARCEL and the edit verbs
packages.design: PK2 is the single owner of command_interpreter.cpp for this programme. Each verb calls the shared parser, takes the words it leaves, resolves them through matchEntities, and puts a 'matched=' record first in its reply. Compatibility defaults: SELECT LAYER x means LAYERS x ONLY, SELECT ALL means DRAWING, LIST defaults to DRAWING, and the transform and attribute verbs default to SELECTION, so no script changes meaning. SELECT keeps isSelectable and counts what that rule leaves out. The transforms leave locked layers and say so. CHLAYER, COLOR, STYLE APPLY and PROP SET/DELETE are re-expressed as planGlobalModify requests, removing their second code path. PROP RENAME waits for PK-S's renameProperties. The AREA verb must decide the clash with the AREA scope keyword (use the WINDOW alias) and must turn an empty scope into '0 matched' before calling computeArea, which refuses an empty list. PARCEL loops over the matched polylines; LABEL for all of them is one step. The survey_workbench Area-of-Selection window change (T10) lives in PK8. Tests go in a new tests/cad/customisation/test_scoped_verbs.cpp (globbed), which avoids the test_cad.cpp hotspot the ui lanes touch, plus cli.* tests. Hotspots: the cli.* tests in src/katana_app/CMakeLists.txt, and the one dispatch line each for PK4's EXPLODE/JOIN/REVERSE/DIVIDE/MEASURE and PK8's POINTS in run(), which PK2 adds on request. Documentation: docs/cad.md.

packages.name: PK-S Extensions to the shared mechanism (for the scope-core owner; gates parts of PK4 and PK6)
packages.design: Hand this to the agent building cad::ModifyScope, ModifyFilter, scope_verbs.hpp and the ScopeFilterWidget, or run it straight after that work lands; these are that agent's files. (1) The parser contract: it returns the words it did not consume, and WHERE ends at a terminator the caller names (SET for MODIFY) or at the end of the line. Verbs whose own options are key=value (LABEL, AUTOLABEL, TEXTEDIT, DIM, GENERATE, PLOT) put those options BEFORE the clause, because WHERE's STYLE= would otherwise swallow LABEL's style=. The scope keyword AREA gets the alias WINDOW for the AREA verb's sake. VIEW comes from a view provider the window sets on the interpreter and is refused headless. (2) One wildcard matcher in core/text.hpp; cad::matchesPattern, entity::globMatches and the tools' matchesWildcard all call it. (3) ModifyFilter gains property comparisons (< > <= >= <>) for Quick Select and CODE= for AUTOLABEL rules and Quick Select. (4) EntityModify gains renameProperties, for PROP RENAME. (5) A scopeSummary helper, so every verb and dialog words 'N matched (of M); K left out because ...' the same way. (6) Confirm T07: MODIFY has VIEW and AREA, and Global Modify runs its line through the runner. (7) Optional: a polygon area, for the legend's rotated windows. Tests go beside the existing global_modify tests.

packages.name: PK3 MCP: scope and where on the entity tools, plus katana_select and katana_modify

JSON' in PK2). katana_describe_entity takes ids[]. katana_export(path, scope, where). New katana_select(scope, where, mode: replace|add|remove) and katana_modify(scope, where, set{...}, preview), whose structured output mirrors GlobalModifyPlan. summary:
Read-only audit of main at 8cd6a7a, plus the 19 ui-gap designs in ui-gap-plan.json and the ui-lane-a work in progress. Nothing was edited, built or committed.

**The finding.** Only MODIFY and the Global Modify dialog act on a scope and a filter today, and even they fall short:
- The MODIFY verb has no VIEW or AREA (command_interpreter.cpp:2660-2676).
- The dialog executes the plan itself instead of building the verb line (global_modify_dialog.cpp:1149-1160).

Every other tool falls into one of three kinds:
- **Selection only:** MOVE, COPY, ROTATE, SCALE, MIRROR, ARRAY, ERASE, CHLAYER, COLOR, STYLE APPLY, PROP, the Attribute Manager and the Layer Manager's move.
- **One id only:** PARCEL, INFO, TEXTEDIT, OFFSET, TRIM, EXTEND.
- **Whole drawing only:** LIST, CLI CODE (it ignores even the selection), EXPORT on the CLI and MCP, AUTOLABEL, LABEL LAYOUT, Surface From Drawing and GENERATE.

**Utility tools, the user's own example.** UTILITY REPORT, VERIFY, CLEARANCE and CHECK read only a CSV schedule (utility_verbs.cpp:81-92), and the dialog cannot even build a line without one. The drawn services also cannot be graded again as they stand: UTILITY DRAW does not write the horizontal and vertical uncertainties, the depth or each segment's path evidence (utility_drawing.cpp:119-147). So a drawing source first needs those properties written back, with a round-trip test that REPORT on the drawing equals REPORT on the file.

**MCP.** Of the 12 tools, katana_list_entities takes no arguments, katana_describe_entity takes one id and katana_export takes a path. There is no select or modify tool with a scope.

**Window-only tools with no verb** (so the CLI and MCP miss them entirely):
- Linework
- Export Survey Points, Point Report, Point Manager
- Quick Select, Select Similar
- Explode, Join, Reverse, Divide, Measure
- Surface From Drawing, Surface From Raster, Surface From Point Cloud

**The interactive tools cannot see the view.** ToolContext carries no view (interactive_tool.hpp:92-102; tool_host.cpp:135). The code itself flags this as outstanding at modify_transform.cpp:290 and 2115 and everyday_support.cpp:142. So a tool's "All" takes layers the view hides, and no tool offers View, Layers or Where.

**Second scope or filter implementations** that CLAUDE.md 1.1 forbids:
- Quick Select's own Condition and wildcard (select_tools.cpp:240-380).
- The label rules' glob matcher (auto_label.cpp:81-110; annotation.cpp:301).
- A third wildcard matcher beside cad::matchesPattern (global_modify.cpp:364).
- SelectionFilter (selection.hpp:19-28).
- ONLINE IMPORT's own `area=` grammar, whose view box ignores rotation (gis_online.cpp:205-240).
- P9's planned "Whole drawing / Current view / Window" combo.

**ui-gap packages that act on drawing data:**
- **Need the shared widget and clause:** P4 Parcel Report, P7 Label Objects and Label Layout Report, P9 Generate, P14 AUTOLABEL run, P17 PLOT and SNAPSHOT, P19 Online area.
- **Exempt:** P2's context menu, which acts on the selection by nature and gains scope through the verbs it runs. P16 STATUS, which is a summary. P3, P5, P6's single text, P8, P10, P11, P12, P13, P15 and P18, which are tables, point-picked or not about entities.

**Also exempt, with the reason:**
- Table verbs (LAYER, LINETYPE, HATCH, STYLE NEW/SET, DIMSTYLE, TEXTSTYLE, LABELSTYLE, PURGE, CRS, ALIGN).
- Point-driven creation (the draw verbs, point-picked DIM kinds, LEADER, BALLOON, FORWARD).
- File-driven work (IMPORT, survey import, traverse, level book).
- Sheet-level work (SHEET, PLOTSHEETS, SHEETS CHECK).
- The Properties panel, which edits the selection; Global Modify is its scope-wide twin.

**Grammar risks the shared parser must settle before the packages start:**
- **WHERE against key=value options.** WHERE's `STYLE=` collides with LABEL's `style=`. The parser should return the words it did not use and end WHERE at a terminator or the end of the line, with a verb's own options placed before the clause.
- **The AREA verb against the AREA scope keyword.** Give the scope keyword the alias WINDOW.
- **SELECT LAYER** must keep meaning the exact layer, so it maps to `LAYERS x ONLY`.
- **SELECT on a scope** must still apply the selectable rule and count locked or hidden entities it leaves out.
- **An empty scope** is reported, not refused. Today AREA's computeArea refuses an empty list.

**Packages**, in order of user value, with disjoint file sets:
- **PK1** utilities act on the drawing.
- **PK2** the interpreter verbs (SELECT, LIST, INFO, transforms, attribute verbs, AREA, PARCEL). It is the single owner of command_interpreter.cpp.
- **PK-S** extensions to the shared mechanism, for the scope-core owner: property comparisons, CODE=, renameProperties, one wildcard matcher, the parser contract and one reply helper. It gates Quick Select, PROP RENAME and the label-rule matcher.
- **PK3** MCP scope and where, plus katana_select and katana_modify.
- **PK4** interactive tools: the view in ToolContext, one scoped selection step, and headless EXPLODE, JOIN, REVERSE, DIVIDE and MEASURE.
- **PK5** EXPORT and POINTS EXPORT.
- **PK6** CODE and a new LINEWORK verb.
- **PK7** annotation.
- **PK8** survey windows.
- **PK9** terrain.
- **PK10** framing: GENERATE, PLOT, SNAPSHOT, ZOOM.
- **PK11** window editors.
- **PK12** Online Data's area.

**Sequencing:**
- **After ui lanes merge:** PK5 needs P12's gis_dialogs.cpp. PK6 builds on P1's survey_code_verbs.cpp. PK7 needs P7 and P14's Qt files. PK8 needs P4. PK10 needs P9 and P17. PK12 needs P19. PK3 also waits for P16.
- **Shared hotspots:** main_window.cpp (small exact edits in PK5, PK6, PK9 and PK10), the cli.* test list in src/katana_app/CMakeLists.txt, and src/katana_cad/CMakeLists.txt:60 for the new utility_source.cpp.

**Open question:** branch utility-scope-core (worktree Katana-wt/uscope-core) had no changes at this audit. Before starting PK1, check whether the scope-core agent is already taking the utility tools.
